environment: isolated gas phase; bare hydride, no counterion or solvent

scfProtocol.stability: internal and external RHF stability checked for every complex frame

pathKind: Four fixed C–H(nu) distance / 110° angle Cs-relaxed frames plus a separately optimized minimum; two matched-distance angle comparisons. Not an IRC. No transition state claimed.
atomMapping: C, O, H1, H2, Hnu fixed identities. C at origin, O on +x, Hnu in xz with z>0; H1/H2 reflected across xz. No post-hoc fit.
competingPathways: Bare gas-phase hydride is an idealized donor, not LiAlH4 or NaBH4. H abstraction (H2 + HCO−), detachment/other electronic states and solvent/counterion chemistry were not compared; the constrained addition branch does not establish global selectivity or kinetics.

grid.fieldPrecision: float32, full float64 SCF coefficients retained

references.difference: rho(current) minus rho(addition-0), on identical Cartesian points. Includes nuclear displacement; not a unique charge-transfer measure.
references.deformation: rho(complex) minus same-geometry Hnu− and neutral H2CO, each in its own RHF/6-31++G(d,p) basis, no ghosts. Fixed atom membership; not counterpoise-corrected EDA.
references.probability: Absolute square of one selected canonical spatial orbital, normalized to 1, without occupation factor.
references.signs: Teal positive / amber negative electron-number difference or orbital amplitude; never positive/negative electrical charge.

initialSelection.protocol: Project hydride occupied 1s and neutral formaldehyde occupied pi / virtual pi* canonical MOs onto full-complex occupied / virtual spaces. Fragment pi references maximize normalized C2pz + O2pz (occupied) or C2pz - O2pz (virtual) AO-trial overlap. These full-complex canonical orbitals are not localized donor/acceptor orbitals.

bondOrderConventions.mayer: sum over AO blocks A/B of (PS)uv(PS)vu, spin-summed RHF P.
bondOrderConventions.lowdinWiberg: sum over AO blocks A/B of |(S^(1/2) P S^(1/2))uv|^2, symmetric positive overlap square root. Not NBO Wiberg; basis and partition dependent.

warnings: METHOD LIMIT: isolated H− is not bound against electron detachment at this HF level (E(H)−E(H−) = -0.011729 Eh). These are finite-basis restricted addition-branch models, not a verified physical gas-phase ground-state path.
title: Carbonyl addition · H⁻ + H₂CO
modelScope: One explicit instance of the unchanged generic R₂C=O + Nu⁻ → R₂C(O⁻)Nu event. Bare gas-phase hydride is not LiAlH₄/NaBH₄; methoxide is before protonation.

energyReference.label: 3.0 Å / 110° constrained complex; not separated reactants

orbitalDefinitions.title: Hydride-projected occupied canonical MO
orbitalDefinitions.description: Initial hydride 1s fragment projection, then tracked canonical complex MO; not localized H⁻.

orbitalDefinitions.title: Carbonyl π-projected occupied canonical MO
orbitalDefinitions.description: Initial formaldehyde π reference, then overlap-tracked complex canonical orbital; its later shape need not remain a pure π bond.

orbitalDefinitions.title: Carbonyl π*-projected virtual canonical MO
orbitalDefinitions.description: Initial formaldehyde π* reference, then tracked complex canonical MO; not a uniquely defined localized acceptor.

series.title: Addition: four constrained frames + verified product minimum

evidence: S1: all complex frames use 18 electrons, singlet RHF; internal and external determinant stability checked. This is a model, not proof against all other electronic states.
O1: hydride 1s / carbonyl π* fragment projections and the computed approach support donor–acceptor interpretation; displayed complex MOs remain canonical.

R1 (existing candidate code): shorter C–H distance accompanies lower C–O Mayer index and density redistribution. Inspect both bond-index conventions; neither is an integer bond count. The code omits the simultaneous π redistribution and numerical bond indices.
G3 (existing candidate code): carbon leaves the O/H1/H2 plane while bonding reorganizes. The defined pyramidalization descriptors quantify what the code omits.
limitations: Bare gas-phase hydride is an idealized donor, not LiAlH4 or NaBH4. H abstraction (H2 + HCO−), detachment/other electronic states and solvent/counterion chemistry were not compared; the constrained addition branch does not establish global selectivity or kinetics.
Only three fixed angles at one distance were compared, with Cs-constrained substrate relaxation. No universal Bürgi–Dunitz angle, optimal trajectory, transition state, barrier or IRC is inferred.

The deformed neutral H2CO fragment can have an external RHF instability; its same-geometry restricted determinant remains the explicitly defined deformation reference, not a verified fragment ground state.
RHF / finite basis; no correlation, solvent, free energy or basis/grid-convergence study. Fragment densities are defined references, not unique charge-transfer partitions.
Uniform display grid is not a quantitative electron-transfer integration grid; normalization uses Tr(PS) and independent level-5 Becke quadrature.
